tagline.text: A marine park on Subic Bay where you watch sea lion and dolphin shows by the water

location.label: Location
location.text: Camayan Point, Subic Bay Freeport (on the border with Morong, Bataan, administratively)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–3,500 (per person, based on transport, admission and meals, excluding encounters)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Clark International Airport (CRK) or Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL)

children.text: Ocean Adventure is a marine animal park in the Subic Bay Freeport that opened in October 2001. Admission includes the sea lion and dolphin shows, an aquarium and a performance introducing Aeta culture. Many families visit on a day trip from Manila.

Ocean Adventure is a marine animal park on the shore at Camayan Point, inside the Subic Bay Freeport. According to Wikipedia and a November 2002 Philstar report, the park opened to the public in October 2001, with the first facilities built for about 7.5 million dollars on the site of a former ammunition pier. In June 2002 the operator, Subic Bay Marine Exploratorium (SBME), signed a 75-year lease with the SBMA that extended the park to the shoreline and waters of Ilanin Bay, including Miracle Beach, which grew the site from about 13 acres to 27 acres. Wikipedia says the park received about 500,000 visitors a year as of 2012 and that in 2017 it was named Best Theme Park at the first Philippine Tourism Industry Awards.

The park's main attraction is its marine animal shows. According to the official website, the headline presentations are Sea Lion Marine Patrol with sea lions, Dolphin Friends with dolphins, and Wild World, which tells a rainforest story together with Aeta traditions, and admission includes all of them. A distinctive feature is watching the dolphin show at an open theater on the water, while the sea lion show is held separately at Sea Lion Point. The aquarium (Ocean Discovery Aquarium) has exhibits of a coral reef, a freshwater stream, mangroves and a dark sea cave, which makes a good rest between shows.

Some encounters cost extra beyond admission. The official website lists programs such as Shark and Turtle Adventure, swimming with dolphins, Sea Lion Paint and Play, Dolphin Beach Encounter (meeting dolphins in shallow water), an exclusive 20-minute session with your own dolphin, and diving with the dolphins. You must check encounter prices separately on the website's reservation page. A 2016 visit report listed rates such as ₱250 for a sea lion photo (2 pictures) and ₱500 for a dolphin photo (2 pictures), which may have changed since. Opinions differ on animal welfare when it comes to contact with animals, so decide for yourself whether to take part.

This guide is for families and couples making a day trip to Subic Bay from Manila or Clark. There is a record that Ocean Adventure had a lease dispute with the SBMA in 2019, closed for seven months in 2020 because of COVID-19, and reopened in October 2020. The official website now says it is open daily, but admission and show times change from year to year, so be sure to check before your visit. Within the same Subic Bay area are the neighboring Camayan Beach Resort and the Adventure Beach Waterpark, and Zoobic Safari is nearby, so many people combine them over two days. It also helps to know the background of the lease dispute. According to Wikipedia and news reports, conflict between the operator and the SBMA continued from the early 2010s and is said to have started with the development of "The Hill," a residential area for expatriates. The SBMA notified the operator of termination of the contract citing illegal subleasing, construction without permits, waste storage problems and closure of public roads, and in October 2019 it seized undeveloped land set aside for expanding the park. The operator asked for negotiations, saying about 500 employees' jobs were at stake. The sources I checked do not clearly say how this dispute was finally settled, but the official website says the park is open daily.

A show in which the sea lions turn into a marine patrol team, and the program kids like best. It is held at Sea Lion Point, and time is sometimes set aside for photos. The schedule changes by season, so ask for it when you enter.

The dolphin show is held in an open sea cove known as the El Capitan Theater. Front seats where water splashes can get you wet, so bring a raincoat or a change of clothes. A camera with zoom helps you shoot from a distance.

A show that tells the story of the Philippine rainforest together with Aeta traditions. Some exotic animals appear alongside. It is a chance to learn about the culture of the Philippines' minority tribes, which also makes it a good educational stop for kids.

An aquarium that recreates a coral reef, a freshwater stream, mangroves and a sea cave. It is not large, but it is a good place to rest and look around during the hot hours. It is included in admission.

Shark and Turtle Adventure, swimming with dolphins, Sea Lion Paint and Play, Dolphin Beach Encounter and others run for a fee. Many programs need reservations, so check availability on the official website before you go. Views on animal welfare differ from person to person.

There is a combined ticket with Adventure Beach Waterpark, which the same operator runs. The official website once listed the combined ticket at ₱1,200, but the current price may change. On a hot day a good plan is to see the park in the morning and move to the waterpark in the afternoon.

Ocean Adventure is an outdoor coastal park, so the dry season from November to May is the most comfortable. March to May is very hot, so it is better to visit in the morning.
In the rainy season (June–October) sudden showers can cancel shows or change their times. The hours the official website gives are daily from 9 AM to 5 PM.

Subic Bay has many hotels and resorts, and Camayan Beach Resort is right next to Ocean Adventure. For a seaside stay choose a place close to the park, and for easy access to town choose Olongapo or the Subic commercial district. Lodging rates vary a great deal by season, so check on a booking site.

There are restaurants and snack sellers inside the park too. One visit report said lunch was not very fresh but was enough to fill you up. Check the rules on bringing outside food when you enter, and it helps to bring snacks and water for the kids. There are also shower facilities and a souvenir shop.

When planning a day, allow plenty of travel time. One visit report said the group hired a driver in Tarlac for ₱3,000 and drove more than 2 hours to get there. If you start from Manila, add the time to change between buses and taxis, so you need to leave early in the morning to arrive by opening time. The park has shower facilities and a souvenir shop, which is handy for washing up after an in-water encounter. If you stay nearby, it is easy to enjoy the shows in the morning and afternoon and return to rest in between. If you bring children, it was reported that there are different rates or free admission for those 12 and under and for children under about 76 cm (30 inches), so check at the entrance.
Entering at opening time helps you avoid the heat and get a front seat at the shows.
Check the schedule you receive at entry and plan the sea lion and dolphin shows so they do not overlap.
If you sit in the front where water splashes, you need a change of clothes and a raincoat.
Bring a hat, sunscreen, water and a zoom camera.
Animal encounters may require reservations, so check the official website before you visit.
Combining the nearby Adventure Beach Waterpark and Zoobic Safari makes for a full day, but it is tight, so splitting them over two days is also a good idea.
There is an environmental fee (about ₱20) paid on site at entry, so bring small change.

A 2016 visit report recommended bringing an umbrella or raincoat and booking tickets early. The park is said to open even in the rain, but on weekends and holidays front seats and encounter reservations fill up early, so a weekday visit is far more relaxed.
Admission, operating hours and show schedules change often. Check the latest information on the official website or by phone before you visit.
This is a facility that keeps marine mammals such as dolphins and sea lions in captivity, so opinions on animal welfare are divided. Decide for yourself whether to take part in contact encounters.
There was a dispute over the lease with the SBMA in 2019, so check the latest operating status.
The sea theater has little shade and the sun is strong. Be sure to bring hats and water for children.
Inside Subic, agree on taxi and tricycle fares in advance to avoid being overcharged.
In the rainy season shows may be canceled or rescheduled, so check the weather.
